newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen sideways in wide price band.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen sideways in wide price band.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE coffee futures are now more likely to trade sideways in a wide $1,700-$2,000 range in the immediate term, technical analysts said on Friday.
The market was due $20-30 higher after slight gains in New York on Thursday, bolstered by a late-session round of commission house and light trade buying.
The activity was mostly locally-oriented. There was no fundamental news behind the move.
Chartwise, analysts said LIFFE's September shaped a positive price action on Thursday as the market continued to look for a meaningful trend.

"The relatively low opening trade closed a previously potentially bullish gap up pattern (at $1,780) which rather takes the wind out of the recovery many technicians expected," said analyst Peter Sceat of MCS Ltd.
"It is now more likely that coffee trades sideways in that wide $1,700-$2,000 band."
"It is fair to say if the recent $1,695 trough were taken out a further sharp fall is likely," he added. September hit a low of $1,695 on June 11.
He pegged resistance at $1,975, followed by $2,005. Support is seen at $1,775, $1,720 and then the major level at $1,695.
On the weather front, no major cold is in sight in Brazil's coffee growing areas in the next three to five days.
Private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said temperatures are forecast near normal on Friday and above normal on Saturday and through to Tuesday.
Conditions are generally favourable for the trees but some disruptions to the harvest are still expected from scattered showers.
